title: Schedule a nightly backup with a systemd user timer
summary: A systemd user timer starts a service at a set time each day, without root rights. You write two short unit files, turn the timer on, then check the next run time and the log.

aliases.text: запуск скрипта каждую ночь без cron

steps.explain: Create the service unit. It says which command to run; %h stands for your home folder. The script from the backup rotation card must be saved as ~/bin/backup-rotate.sh first.
steps.cmd:
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user && cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/backup-home.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nightly incremental backup of my documents

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=%h/bin/backup-rotate.sh <SRC_DIR> <DEST_ROOT> 7
EOF

placeholders.name: SRC_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder you want to back up

placeholders.name: DEST_ROOT
placeholders.description: Folder on the backup drive that holds all snapshots

steps.explain: Create the timer unit. It starts the service every night at 02:30. Persistent=true runs a missed night's job at the next start of the computer.
steps.cmd:
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user && cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/backup-home.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Run the nightly backup at 02:30

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:30:00
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=10min

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF

steps.explain: Check both unit files for errors without starting anything. A warning that a file in ExecStart is not executable only means the script is not saved in ~/bin yet.
steps.expect: No output, or only the warning about the missing script.

steps.explain: Load the new units and turn the timer on so it starts now and at every boot.
Show when the next run is due. The NEXT column must show tomorrow at 02:30 or later.
steps.expect: One row for backup-home.timer with a NEXT time at 02:30.

steps.explain: Let the user timers run while you are logged out. Without this the timer only runs during a login session. Some systems ask for an administrator password here.
Run the backup once now and read the log, so you do not have to wait for the night.
steps.expect: Lines of rsync output, then a 'Finished' line with the description. 'Failed with result' means the run went wrong.

rollback.explain: Turn the timer off and stop it right away.
Delete both unit files and reload the user manager.
Optional: stop user timers from running after logout.

warnings: The backup runs without you watching. Check that the destination drive is mounted before the run, or the backup lands in an empty folder on the system disk.
Enable-linger lets your user services run while nobody is logged in. Disable it if you do not want that.
